source_scope_note: 21 concrete source files/ranges independently read; other author records were checked for scoped provenance and consistency, not represented as another whole-repository audit.

findings.problem: ErrorRecord short-prefix/struct_size semantics did not specify complete storage preconditions, write extent, or whether diagnostics could replace the original failure status.
findings.resolution: Strict 24-byte v1 record; optional null output; nonnull at least initialized four-byte header; capacity0-23 no writes/original status retained; capacity>=24 writes exactly24 with size24 and flags0, preserves tail; OK/PENDING no writes; checked before full-struct reference; ER-01 canary matrix.

findings.problem: Generic CALLBACK_FAILED failure mapping could publish a second terminal or rewrite an already committed native outcome/Unknown remote effect, contradicting D06.
findings.resolution: Decision/ordinary/terminal roles separated. Terminal callback uses preallocated managed fault latch and existing cleanup slot; immutable native outcome/effect retained; once-only take/forfeit plus full retire/drain continues.

findings.problem: Unqualified get_api language implied a mandatory module function table, conflicting with D02 direct exports and minimal adapter goal.
findings.resolution: Direct exports remain default; get_api only for explicit optional profile. Start callback table is distinguished; payload bytes use the common uint64/ulong wire width.

findings.problem: Residual prefix-extension and conditional hot-unload wording could be misread as weakening the fixed-v1 record and permanently loaded module decisions.
findings.resolution: Section10 now explicitly points to full-v1 capacity rules; new fields require new ABI/capability. Section8 prohibits v1 module unload and limits the stated quiescence requirement to a future separately designed profile.

evidence_interpretation: Main fixture genuinely executed normal10528/AOT10529 assertions,32 callback rounds per profile on Windows/Linux; one native Rust unit test,9 Roslyn assertions,4/6 restrictions assertions are scoped tests.
10,000 deterministic arithmetic cases compare against BigInteger; repeated assertions or operating systems do not become independent protocols or a production test suite.

Supplemental csbindgen source-generated calls agree with direct LibraryImport for60 normal+60AOT cases, and unsupported tuple omission is real. This compares bindings, not two independent native implementations.

Seven Rust panic child cases preserve two surviving and five unsuccessful process outcomes; invalid UCO normal/AOT failed before body with unhandled InvalidProgramException; no outer-catch recovery was tested.
Main native fixture uses private statuses; its blocking callback is a deliberate test barrier, not a production callback implementation.
Mailbox/retirement models cover stated finite sequentially consistent abstractions. Loom/Kani/Miri and broad fuzz/sanitizers were not falsely claimed executed.
Original source_commit null fields and Windows CRLF source identities remain unchanged; CI archive metadata plus verified source bytes bind the published experiment commit.

R02: Clean Rust-free NuGet consumer and complete supported RID matrix in A14/A15/A21; linker and metadata negative gates in real packages.
R03: Complete generated C/Rust/C# size/offset/version/unknown-capability golden matrix in A01/A02/A12; unsupported RID remains unsupported until executed.
R04: Measured transition/copy/allocation costs on product kernels in R30/A21; Direct P/Invoke loader paths and whole callback signature diagnostic suite in A12/A14/A15.
R05: Production generator inventory/hash gate, package reproducibility and all unsupported signatures in A09-A12; alternative repositories are scoped comparisons, not adopted product dependencies.
R06: Production IDE/CLI/multi-target snapshot, diagnostic span, incremental performance and package consumption tests in A10-A12/B10/B12.
R07: Complete product parent/child transfer, mutable builder writer, finalizer and worker-affine cleanup matrices in A03/A04/A20/B01; weak-memory proof at actual atomics.
R08: Full product registration generations, dispatcher saturation/reentrancy and long concurrent unregister matrix in A06/A20/B14; prototype is not the product scheduler.
R09: Every setup failure/control lease/take/quarantine interleaving mapped to implementation in A07/A19/A20; no progress under permanently stopped executor is promised.
R10: Product backing-byte/pin/held-result budget accounting, zero-copy eligibility and retained-buffer memory load in A04/A20/B15/B22; no whole-RSS bound inferred.
R11: Complete Engine poison/supervisor/error mapping/allocator failure tests and Windows fatal fixtures in A05/A14/A15/A20; unknown damaged resources stay quarantined.
R12: Product waiter/permit/cleanup budget and weak-memory lost-wake tests; engine close OS-thread join, fairness and long shutdown loads in A08/A18/B22.
R15: Loom/Kani/Miri execution only when actual product code is mapped to stated properties; report exact bound/coverage/fairness and negative control in A19/A20.
R16: Product coverage-guided fuzz corpus, applicable sanitizer builds, all-RID artifact replay, real DB/network differential and sustained failure stress in A20/B22.

acceptance_reasoning: Mature framework imports, Rust Engine ownership and narrow adapters satisfy source-driven reuse without a global Core runtime.
Logical admission, physical SafeHandle lease, native/managed quiescence, result ownership and remote effect are explicitly distinct and match source counterexamples.
Errors/cancellation/cleanup are specified at the ABI and wrapper boundary with finite test oracles; no future product completion is required to accept the design that guides it.
Versioned contracts and delivery obligations can now be accepted at design scope after the resolved independent findings.
